# Statement ledger

This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
the manuscript revision a284420, and labels are written exactly as in its
LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98, 3920258 and
975feb3. Revision a284420 makes two mathematical edits that the ledger
follows. (1) In `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` it adds Lemma
`L:spatial-fourier-bound` (lines 101-164, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound`),
the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_alpha b^(alpha/2)` that
`SpatialFourierBound` already proved, and the proof of
`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (same label and statement) now derives `R_0 < inf`
from it, independently of the finiteness of `S_1^pos`, which it keeps only
for the score inequality. (2) In the main file, `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
replaces its smoothing and truncation sentence by the multiplier comparison
`E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (a measurable multiplier `m` in `[0,1]`,
nested measurable Laplace domains, positivity after time integration,
scaling asserted only for the original covariance) and its proof by the
corresponding argument. The other changes since 975feb3 are prose and front
matter (title, abstract, preface, a theory-outlook chapter, the reader
edition, Appendices F and G, the list of notation moved to the back).
Every cited label exists exactly once at a284420. Three of them are new at
a284420 and do not exist at 975feb3: `L:spatial-fourier-bound`,
`E:spatial-fourier-bound` and `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`. Every other
cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at both revisions, and
every such cited lemma, proposition, theorem, equation and section has the
same statement and proof up to whitespace and braces, except
`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (proof only), `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
(statement and proof) and the section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
(the new lemma). TeX line numbers were moved to a284420 by a line map; each
moved range has the same text at both revisions, and the ranges inside the
two edited passages were mapped to the corresponding new passages by hand
(script checks recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).

## Scope

- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean` (step modules) or
  `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/<Module>.lean` (library modules: whole results, narrower results, foundations and proof steps);
  `Audit/<module>/` prints the elaborated types.
- The rows cover every public theorem (2050) and 418 definitions whose
  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other 89
  public definitions have no rows of their own: 85 (for example `kappa`,
  `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`, `InventoryProduct.partialEval`,
  `OccupationPhysicalClass.volI`, `SpaceTimePositivity.timeMeasure`,
  `TerminalWick.chainMassReal`, `WaveGreenFourier.spherePhi` and
  `OccupationCeilingExact.stepG`) only name quantities or measures used in
  those statements, and four are the instances that make
  `TimeCompletion.Pre` a pre-inner-product space; read their bodies in the
  Lean source or in `Audit/`.
- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
  inner-product and finite-word facts. The exception is `HermiteWordFock`
  (wave L9), which applies `HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw` to the Fock model of
  `FockForm` and so formalizes the special case of `L:finite-word-cutoff`
  with one Gaussian coordinate per color (section "HermiteWordFock (narrower result: `L:finite-word-cutoff` for one Gaussian mode per color and single finite words; finite sums and Bochner integrals not formalized)"); the
  multi-mode case is not formalized.
- Section headings use three categories. (A) "whole result": every
  conclusion of the labelled result is a Lean conclusion under the
  manuscript's hypotheses, possibly with named supplied inputs that are
  disclosed (coverage class same-assumptions or inputs-supplied, conclusion
  full); no other section carries it. (B) "narrower result: ...": a labelled
  result some of whose conclusions are not Lean conclusions, or are proved
  for a modelled object (the class `O` by joint representatives, the rate in
  Rayleigh form, the cost in integral form, an abstract structure standing
  for an object the manuscript constructs, an object that is not constructed)
  whose identification with the manuscript's object is not formalized; the
  heading names what is missing. The one exception is a registered model
  choice (next item): a result whose only modelled object is such a choice
  stays a whole result, and its section names the model.
  Discharging a named input in a completion module does not turn a narrower
  result into a whole one. (C) "foundation: ..." or "proof steps ...": facts
  used by labelled results, not a labelled result themselves; every
  `StratonovichHAMAudit` section except `HermiteWordFock` is of this kind.
  The first cell of an Index row uses the same words.
- Model-choice register. A registered model choice is a documented
  definitional choice that is the standard construction of a manuscript
  object, recorded with the identification that is not formalized. M1 (wave
  L6, Le's decision 4): the wave Green measure in `d = 3` is
  `(s/(4 pi)) map (omega -> s omega) volume.toSphere`, Mathlib's sphere
  measure scaled to the radius-`s` sphere; its identification with the
  surface (Hausdorff or Riemannian) measure of the TeX is not proved. Results
  whose only modelled object is M1 (`L:low-alpha-convolution`,
  `L:phase-contractions`, and the sections `LowAlphaConvolution`,
  `PhaseContractions` and `L9Completed`) are whole results. Missing
  constructions are not model choices: they make a result narrower (for
  example the noise `W` of `P:masked-quotient-obstruction`, the ground
  family of `L:raw-block-indexed-cone`, the chain measures used for
  `L:uniform-series-tail`, the operator paths of `P:radius-mean-anchor`, the
  solution moments of `P:moment-growth-logconvex` and
  `C:static-moment-constant-continuity`).
- The seventy-six `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` modules: 27 are whole-result
  modules (all with nothing supplied), 31 are narrower-result modules, and 18 are foundations or proof steps (`WaveKernel`,
  `SpectralHomog`, `TimeFractional`, `DampedNorms`, `GaussianIBP`,
  `GaussianTest`, `WeakSobolev`, `VariationalFloor`, `SeriesType`,
  `H1Density`, `FiniteWick`, `GaussianHermite`, `HermiteFock`, `WaveGreen`,
  `WaveGreenFourier`, `SpaceTimePositivity`, `IntervalScalar`,
  `StaticPhaseCauchy`). Some modules without a section of their own are
  covered in the section of the module they serve. Together they model
  `H:homog` and give, by labelled result, 25 whole results (with the
  manuscript's hypotheses alone; none remains whole with named inputs), 18
  narrower results with the manuscript's hypotheses, and steps or parts of
  30 further results
  (see `COMPLETION.md`), to the scopes specified below (the narrower
  conclusions are stated per result). Forty-seven (the 25 whole and 18
  narrower results with the manuscript's hypotheses, and
  `E:kappa` and `E:driver-parameters`, `E:masked-time-schur` and
  `R:gaussian-one-variance-test`) need no supplied input:
  `L:gaussian-scalar-powers` is stated with the manuscript's own hypotheses.
  `L:gram-scalar-algebra` and `L:tube-rayleigh-tail` are proved under weaker
  hypotheses (no completeness or `C_ij >= 0`; no `delta < 1`) and also

# Formalization scope

## The paper's argument and where Lean enters

The paper bounds and identifies the growth of `log E[u(t,x)²]` for the
Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model. The argument has three layers.

1. **Stochastic and analytic layer.** The chaos expansion, the two-chain
   pairing integrals, Wick pairings (beyond finite families of Gaussian
   values), Gaussian integration (beyond finitely many standard Gaussians),
   imported bounds,
   Laplace transforms and the variational asymptotics. **Not in Lean**,
   except a few slices: the Laplace transforms of the wave kernel and of
   the two-time kernel and the subordination formula (`ClockCopy` and its
   foundation modules), the Gaussian transform of the spectral measure
   (`MaskedSpectralGrowth`), the uniform scalar frequency row
   (`FrequencyRow`), the temporal completion `H_a` (`TimeCompletion`), the
   auxiliary mask norm (`MaskedAuxiliaryNorm`), the Gaussian heat envelope
   of the covariance (`VariationalMean`), a finite Hilbert-valued Bessel
   inequality (`PhaseBessel`), the wave Green measures `G_s` for
   `d = 1, 2, 3` (`WaveGreen`), the spectral identity and positive
   definiteness of `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` (`QuotientObstruction`), a
   finite Gaussian comparison under the positive semidefinite order
   (`GaussianComparison`), the two wave variance directions in spectral
   form (`WaveTwoVariances`), the variational floor and the Rayleigh-form
   rate (`VariationalFloor`, `VariationalRate`), the deterministic Fourier
   bound `L:spatial-fourier-bound` for the smooth spatial ratio and the
   static controls
   (`SpatialFourierBound`, `SpatialSmoothRatio`, `SpatialStaticControls`,
   `SpatialOccupationCompleted`), series types and the continuity of the
   growth types in the temporal exponent (`SeriesType`, `TypeContinuity`),
   the white-noise bound formulas and clock transforms
   (`WhiteRelativeWidth`, `WhiteClockLaplace`), the coefficient bound of
   the interval inventory product (`InventoryProduct`), an abstract `L^2`
   limit of a regularized series under a uniform scaled moment bound
   (`UniformSeriesTail`), the density of test functions in the
   weak-gradient `H^1` (`H1Density`), the physical four-linear extension
   and the spatial energy (`SpatialFourLinear`), the full physical
   occupation class (`OccupationPhysicalClass`; both completed in
   `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`), the scalar and Hilbert-space steps
   of the static interaction and interval coefficient bounds
   (`IntervalScalar`, `IntervalScalarCompleted`), the spectral-mass
   identity `R_Gamma(1) = R_alpha` (`SpectralMassIdentity`), Gaussian
   smoothing as a Fourier multiplier (`DampedMultiplier`), the positivity of
   the space-time occupation form, the deterministic occupation ceiling and
   the spatial bracket (`SpaceTimePositivity`, `OccupationCeilingFinite`,
   `SpatialBracket`, completed in `L8Completed`), the masked rates
   (`RemoveMask`), the finite Wick formula and the terminal-chain Wick
   formula with the chain measures given by their masses (`FiniteWick`,
   `TerminalWick`), an abstract compact Young baseline (`SymplecticFree`)
   and the Cauchy steps of the static phase orders (`StaticPhaseCauchy`),
   the Fourier transforms of the wave Green measures in `d = 1, 2, 3` and
   Archimedes' law for the sphere measure (`WaveGreenFourier`), the low-alpha
   convolution bound and the static contraction bounds
   (`LowAlphaConvolution`, `PhaseContractions`, completed in `L9Completed`),
   the exact occupation constant and ceiling (`RawOccupationEnergy`,
   `OccupationCeilingExact`), the normalized Hermite polynomials and the
   finite Gaussian Fock layer with values in a Hilbert factor
   (`GaussianHermite`, `HermiteFock`) and their consumers `L:fock-form`,
   `L:interval-contractions` and `E:occupied-multiplication` (`FockForm`),
   and the scalar and numerical-range steps of the complex phase bounds
   (`ComplexPhaseScalar`).
2. **Reductions to explicit inequalities.** At many points the analytic
   argument reduces to a finite statement: an exponent range, an exact
   rational or square-root inequality, a polynomial that must stay positive
   on a region, a determinant or matrix inverse, a count of coefficients in
   a finite word, or an integral comparison once integrability is known.
   **These are what Lean checks.**
3. **Assembly** of the main theorems from the layers above. **Not in Lean.**

So each module checks one reduction in layer 2. Its hypotheses state the
facts that layer 1 supplies (for example positivity of a parameter,
integrability of a function, or an inequality proved analytically in the
paper). Its conclusion is the fact that the paper then uses.

## Status of each kind of statement

| Kind | Count | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Whole result (ledger heading "whole result"), nothing supplied | 25 labelled results, `H:homog`, `E:kappa`, `E:driver-parameters`, `E:masked-time-schur` and `R:gaussian-one-variance-test`; 27 modules: 559 theorems, 135 definitions | Every conclusion of the result is a Lean conclusion under the manuscript's hypotheses (`H:homog` modelled in full; most results via exact-hypothesis wrappers); coverage class same-assumptions, conclusion full |
| Whole result, inputs supplied | none: the three results formerly here (`P:radius-mean-anchor`, `P:moment-growth-logconvex`, `C:static-moment-constant-continuity`) are proved for abstract objects whose construction is missing, so they are narrower results | — |
| Narrower result (ledger heading "narrower result: ...", naming what is missing) | 18 results with the manuscript's hypotheses and steps or parts of 30 further results; 31 modules and the audit file `HermiteWordFock`: 943 theorems, 199 definitions | Kernel-checked; some conclusion of the result is not a Lean conclusion. The 18 with the manuscript's hypotheses (coverage same-assumptions, weaker): `P:masked-quotient-obstruction` for the covariance functional (the noise `W` not constructed), `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` with its closing smoothing remark in a narrower reading (covariance smoothing only as membership of the Gaussian multiplier, without its spectral identification; the Green-smoothing identification is proved in `d = 1, 2, 3`), the Rayleigh lemma without its application, the dilation lemma for the integral-form cost, `P:masked-auxiliary-norm` without its clause for a real `H`, `L:variational-global-mean` without the mixed-derivative bounds, `P:variational-unmasked-rate` without its operator half, `L:spatial-static-controls`, `P:spatial-smooth-ratio` and `P:spatial-energy-map` for the Rayleigh-form rate and the integral-form cost, `P:spatial-four-linear` with the joint continuity of `C_4` in sequential form, `P:occupation-physical-class` over the class `O` modelled by joint representatives, `P:variational-positive-scores` without `Q_2 >= S_2^pos`, `T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling` with the exact `C_occ` in both forms over the modelled class `O`, without `C_2 <= U_2`, `C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket` for `S_2^pos` in place of `C_2`, `L:positive-raw-embedding` in integral form (variance identity, row and Schur bounds), and `P:raw-occupation-energy` and `L:occupation-rayleigh-selection` over the class `O` modelled by joint representatives. The 30 further results (coverage inputs-supplied, weaker) have analytic inputs supplied or only some conclusions formalized: `P:radius-mean-anchor` for abstract random paths (the operator paths `M_R(Y_m)` not constructed), `P:moment-growth-logconvex` and `C:static-moment-constant-continuity` for an abstract moment function (the solution moments not constructed), `L:raw-block-indexed-cone` for an abstract ground family, `L:uniform-series-tail` for an abstract `L^2` family (chain measures fixed only by their masses), the finite comparison of `P:masked-noise-completion`, `P:wave-two-variances` with named inputs (spectral core with none), `P:interval-coefficients` with named inputs, `P:variational-remove-mask` (rates with none, the point display over a named input), `L:terminal-wick` (named measurability input, chain measures by their masses), `L:symplectic-free` (free group and Young convergence supplied), `L:fock-form` and `L:interval-contractions` (spatial column bound supplied), the scalar steps of `L:complex-phase` and `L:interval-complex`, `L:finite-word-cutoff` for one Gaussian mode per color, and the others listed in `coverage.yaml` |
| Foundation or proof steps (ledger heading "foundation: ..." or "proof steps of ...") | 18 modules: 466 theorems, 78 definitions | Kernel-checked facts used by labelled results, not a labelled result themselves: `WaveKernel`, `SpectralHomog`, `TimeFractional`, `DampedNorms`, `GaussianIBP`, `GaussianTest`, `WeakSobolev`, `VariationalFloor`, `SeriesType`, `H1Density`, `FiniteWick`, `GaussianHermite`, `HermiteFock`, `WaveGreen`, `WaveGreenFourier`, `SpaceTimePositivity`, and the proof steps `IntervalScalar` (the steps of `C:static-interaction`, with `E:static-block-series` in full) and `StaticPhaseCauchy` (the Cauchy steps of `P:static-phase-all-orders`), whose analytic inputs are supplied |
| Checked step fact (`StratonovichHAMAudit/`, except `HermiteWordFock`) | 82 theorems, 6 definitions | Kernel-checked; the ledger gives its paper label and outside inputs |
| of which helper lemmas (`internal`) | 847 theorems, 51 definitions | Kernel-checked; used inside one module |
| Other public definitions | 89 | Named quantities and measures used in the statements (85), and four instances on `TimeCompletion.Pre` |
| Negative controls | 68 | Wrong variants that Lean must reject |
| Refutations | 235 | Lean proofs refuting specified variants of declarations: manuscript scalar steps, Lean-route-only constructions, and controls of totalized arithmetic or of broader generalizations (the ledger states each one's domain) |

Heading categories (the same three are used in the statement ledger and in
every first cell of its Index by label). The ledger Scope keeps the
model-choice register. M1, its only entry, is the `d = 3` wave Green measure
`(s/(4 pi)) map (omega -> s omega) volume.toSphere` (wave L6, decision 4);
its identification with the surface measure of the TeX is not proved. A
registered standard choice preserves whole status only when the result's
section names the model (as `LowAlphaConvolution`, `PhaseContractions` and
`L9Completed` do for M1); a missing construction (the noise `W`, an abstract
ground family, chain measures fixed by their masses, abstract random paths,
an abstract moment function) makes the result narrower.
(A) "whole result": every conclusion of the labelled result is a Lean
conclusion under the manuscript's hypotheses, possibly with named supplied
inputs that are disclosed (coverage class same-assumptions or
inputs-supplied, conclusion full; at present every whole result has the
manuscript's hypotheses alone); no other module carries it. (B) "narrower
result: ...": a labelled result some of whose conclusions are not Lean
conclusions, or are proved for a modelled object (such as the class `O` by
joint representatives, or the rate in Rayleigh form and the cost in integral
form) whose identification with the manuscript's object is not formalized;
the heading names what is missing. (C) "foundation: ..." or "proof steps of
...": facts used by labelled results, not a labelled result themselves; the
`StratonovichHAMAudit` step modules are all of this kind.

Modules are counted by their ledger heading; a module that also proves
pieces of other results is counted once. Completion modules
(`ClockCopyHomog`, `MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted`, `L9Completed`,
`SpatialOccupationCompleted`, `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`,
`IntervalScalarCompleted`, `L8Completed`) discharge named inputs of other
modules; discharging an input does not make a narrower result whole, so
`L8Completed` (narrower results, including `L:uniform-series-tail` with the
chain measures fixed only by their masses) and the spatial and occupation
modules remain "narrower result". `ClockCopyHomog`,
`MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted` and `TimeSchur`, which have no section of
their own, count as whole-result modules; `DampedNorms`, `SpectralHomog`,
`TimeFractional`, `WaveKernel`, `GaussianIBP`, `GaussianTest` and
`WeakSobolev` as foundations.

These counts describe the package. They are not a percentage of the paper.
The 25 whole results and 18 narrower results with the manuscript's
hypotheses are deterministic lemmas,
propositions and corollaries used inside the analytic argument, and the
occupation ceiling `T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling` (a narrower result: both
forms with the exact constant, for `S_c^pos`; `C_2 <= U_2` not formalized);
the other three main theorems are not formalized.

## Reading a statement

For each declaration, check three things against the paper:

1. the hypotheses match what the paper has available at that point;
2. the conclusion is what the paper uses next;
3. parameter ranges, strict versus non-strict inequalities and quantifier
   order agree.

The [statement ledger](docs/statement-ledger.md) records this for every row.
`Audit/<module>/` prints the full elaborated types, so the statements can be
read without opening an editor.

## Not yet included

Three development modules use a Gaussian-chaos library that is not yet
public: normalized Gaussian coordinates, vector Gaussian projection and
colored vector words. They are checked in the private development record
and will be added here when that library is released.

## Possible next steps

- the finite pair-partition counts behind the two-chain integrals;
- a reusable Laplace-to-time growth lemma, with its analytic inputs as
  hypotheses;
- the constant and exponent algebra of the main upper and lower bounds.

   109	the heading names what is missing. (C) "foundation: ..." or "proof steps of
   110	...": facts used by labelled results, not a labelled result themselves; the
   111	`StratonovichHAMAudit` step modules are all of this kind.
   112	
   113	Modules are counted by their ledger heading; a module that also proves
   114	pieces of other results is counted once. Completion modules
   115	(`ClockCopyHomog`, `MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted`, `L9Completed`,
   116	`SpatialOccupationCompleted`, `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`,
   117	`IntervalScalarCompleted`, `L8Completed`) discharge named inputs of other
   118	modules; discharging an input does not make a narrower result whole, so
   119	`L8Completed` (narrower results, including `L:uniform-series-tail` with the
   120	chain measures fixed only by their masses) and the spatial and occupation
   121	modules remain "narrower result". `ClockCopyHomog`,
   122	`MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted` and `TimeSchur`, which have no section of
   123	their own, count as whole-result modules; `DampedNorms`, `SpectralHomog`,
   124	`TimeFractional`, `WaveKernel`, `GaussianIBP`, `GaussianTest` and
   125	`WeakSobolev` as foundations.

   127	These counts describe the package. They are not a percentage of the paper.
   128	The 25 whole results and 18 narrower results with the manuscript's
   129	hypotheses are deterministic lemmas,
   130	propositions and corollaries used inside the analytic argument, and the
   131	occupation ceiling `T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling` (a narrower result: both
   132	forms with the exact constant, for `S_c^pos`; `C_2 <= U_2` not formalized);
   133	the other three main theorems are not formalized.

   135	## Reading a statement
   136	
   137	For each declaration, check three things against the paper:
   138	
   139	1. the hypotheses match what the paper has available at that point;
   140	2. the conclusion is what the paper uses next;
   141	3. parameter ranges, strict versus non-strict inequalities and quantifier
   142	   order agree.
   143	
   144	The [statement ledger](docs/statement-ledger.md) records this for every row.
   145	`Audit/<module>/` prints the full elaborated types, so the statements can be
   146	read without opening an editor.

   148	## Not yet included
   149	
   150	Three development modules use a Gaussian-chaos library that is not yet
   151	public: normalized Gaussian coordinates, vector Gaussian projection and
   152	colored vector words. They are checked in the private development record
   153	and will be added here when that library is released.

  803| \begin{lemma}[Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails]
  804|   \label{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}
  805|   Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, the integrals
  806|   in~\eqref{E:damped-norm-definitions} are finite for every $\theta > 0$, with
  807|   $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$, and
  808|   \[
  809|     N_0(\theta)=\theta^{-2},\qquad
  810|     N_1(\theta)=\theta^{\alpha+\alpha_0-2}N_1(1),\qquad
  811|     N_2(\theta)^2=\theta^{-\beta}N_2(1)^2,
  812|     \quad\beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0.
  813|   \]
  814|   Let
  815|   \[
  816|     K_M(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
  817|     \int_M^\infty e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
  818|   \]
  819|   Denote by $N_1^{(M)}(1)$ the first norm with $\lambda > M$, and by
  820|   $N_2^{(M)}(1)$ the second norm with $K_M(s-t)$ in place of
  821|   $|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}$. Then
  822|   \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-tail-norms}
  823|     N_1^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0,\qquad
  824|     N_2^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0\quad(M\to\infty).
  825|   \end{equation}
  826|   More precisely, let $m:\R^d\to[0,1]$ be measurable and let
  827|   $S\subset S'\subset(0,\infty)$ be measurable. Define $N_{1,m,S}(\theta)$
  828|   by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$ and restricting the $\lambda$ integral in
  829|   $N_1$ to $S$. Define $N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2$ by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$
  830|   and the temporal kernel in $N_2^2$ with
  831|   \[
  832|     K_S(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
  833|     \int_S e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
  834|   \]
  835|   Then, for every $\theta>0$,
  836|   \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-multiplier-comparison}
  837|     \begin{split}
  838|       0\le N_{1,m,S}(\theta)&\le N_{1,1,S'}(\theta),\\
  839|       0\le N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2&\le N_{2,1,S'}(\theta)^2.
  840|     \end{split}
  841|   \end{equation}
  842|   These are comparisons of spectral expressions, including full and tail
  843|   domains. An arbitrary $m$ need not preserve Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}; the
  844|   scaling identities above are asserted for the original covariance only.
  845|   Spatial Gaussian smoothing and Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel
  846|   give multipliers in this class. The separate mass identity for $N_0$ is
  847|   unchanged by Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel.

 2009| \begin{remark}[Limitation of the uniform pairing estimate]\label{R:G0-verdict}
 2010|   Since $\beta > 2$, we have $1 < \rho < 2$. Thus, Proposition~\ref{P:envelope}
 2011|   improves the crude quadratic time scale under homogeneity. It does not itself
 2012|   prove Theorem~\ref{T:intro-upper}; Section~\ref{S:interval-upper} uses a different
 2013|   argument. Theorem~3.1 used through its uniform pairing estimate is \emph{not
 2014|   sufficient to prove Theorem~\ref{T:intro-upper}}: even with exact homogeneous norm scaling, the
 2015|   resulting majorant has exponent $\rho > \kappa$. The order coefficient has
 2016|   factorial denominator $(k!)^{3-\alpha-\alpha_0}$, whereas the desired scale
 2017|   requires $(k!)^{3-\alpha}$; the missing factor is $(k!)^{\alpha_0}$, up to
 2018|   exponential factors in $k$. Counting the $2k+1$ chain-length splits does not
 2019|   cause this loss, since it can be absorbed into an exponential factor. This
 2020|   conclusion does not rule out a more refined application retaining temporal
 2021|   order or grouping pairings before estimating them, and does not disprove the
 2022|   conjecture. In the formal boundary limit $\alpha_0\downarrow0$, both $\rho$
 2023|   and $\kappa$ tend to $(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)$. This necessary time-independent
 2024|   calibration does not distinguish them and asserts no endpoint theorem or
 2025|   uniformity of constants in $\alpha_0$. At $p = 1$ use the empty-chain case
 2026|   with $e^{\theta t}$ in place of $e^{2\theta t}$; minimizing at $\theta = \beta
 2027|   k/t$ changes only a constant to the power $k$, leaving the same factorial
 2028|   denominator $(k!)^{3-\alpha-\alpha_0}$. It therefore also loses the factorial
 2029|   power $\alpha_0$ relative to $\beta/\kappa = 3-\alpha$, the power
 2030|   corresponding to the target series scale. This is a comparison of scales, not
 2031|   a coefficient estimate asserted by the source's Theorem~1.2. The loss is not
 2032|   specific to the second moment. Both the crude and homogeneous upper bounds are
 2033|   consistent with the Jensen lower bound, being at larger time scales. No
 2034|   identification with the Skorohod second moment is used: its exclusion of
 2035|   self-pairings changes the combinatorics, already visible in the $(0,2)$ and
 2036|   $(2,0)$ terms of Lemma~\ref{L:white-test}.
 2037| \end{remark}

 2289|   Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $A_0$ a bounded nonnegative selfadjoint
 2290|   operator, and $B$ a bounded selfadjoint operator. Write $A_\rho = \rho^2+A_0$.
 2291|   Suppose that, for $0 < a < 1$ and $d > 0$,
 2292|   \begin{equation}\label{E:abstract-sandwich}
 2293|     \|A_\rho^{-1/2}BA_\rho^{-1/2}\|\le d\rho^{a-2},
 2294|     \qquad \rho>0.
 2295|   \end{equation}
 2296|   Put
 2297|   \[
 2298|     I_a=\int_0^\infty s^{-1/2}(1+s)^{(a-3)/2}\ud s,\qquad
 2299|     \delta_a=\min\{1/4,\pi/(8I_a)\}.
 2300|   \]
 2301|   For $\lambda > 0$ and $|z| \le \delta_a\lambda^{2-a}/d$, let $L = A_0-zB$. The
 2302|   phase propagator of $u''+Lu = 0$ satisfies
 2303|   \begin{equation}\label{E:complex-phase-bound}
 2304|     \|\mathcal{M}_z(h)\|_{X_\lambda\to X_\lambda}
 2305|     \le100e^{2\lambda h},\qquad
 2306|     \|(f,g)\|_{X_\lambda}^2
 2307|     =\|f\|^2+\|A_\lambda^{-1/2}g\|^2,\quad h\ge0.
 2308|   \end{equation}
 2309|   The constant is independent of $H$, $\|A_0\|$ and $\|B\|$.
 2310| \end{lemma}

1	\section{Physical spatial pairings and the full occupation class}
     2	\label{S:spatial-occupation-foundation}
     3	
     4	Retain a nonzero original covariance from Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} with its
     5	amplitude. Set $a = \alpha_0$, $k = 3-\alpha > 1$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $D =
     6	q-2a > 0$. The scalar $D$ is fixed. All profiles are real. The original positive
     7	temporal exponent and threshold imply $\alpha < 2$; this is the strict
     8	inequality used in the scalar powers and concavity. The finite variational value
     9	over nonnegative controls $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is that of
    10	Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores}.
    11	
    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is
    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-physical-pair}
    16	    B_\Gamma(f,h)=\int f(x)h(x-y)\nu(\ud x,\ud y)
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
    20	  Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.
    22	\end{lemma}
    23	
    24	\begin{proof}
    25	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ gives sigma-finiteness on exhausting balls, and
    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.
    33	\end{proof}
    34	
    35	Put $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) = B_\Gamma(g^2,g^2)$ and $b(g) = \|\nabla g\|_2^2$ on
    36	$H^1$; initially $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is used only for smooth compact profiles
    37	before the extension below. For smooth compact $z$, write $U_z = \Gamma*z$ in
    38	its usual pointwise sense.
    39	
    40	\begin{lemma}[Smooth temporal controls]\label{L:spatial-static-controls}
    41	  For every nonnegative nonzero $z \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$, let
    42	  \[
    43	    \lambda_z(c)^2=
    44	    \sup_{\substack{g\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|g\|_2=1}}
    45	    \left(c\int U_zg^2-b(g)\right),\qquad c>0.
    46	  \]
    47	  This is positive and finite, and $\lambda_z$ is Lipschitz on every compact
    48	  positive $c$ interval. With the exact $M_a$
    49	  in~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-mass},
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-score}
    51	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
    52	    \lambda_z(1)-\frac{M_a}{2}B_\Gamma(z,z).
    53	  \end{equation}
    54	\end{lemma}
    55	
    56	\begin{proof}
    57	  Choose nonnegative nonzero $f \in C_c^\infty(0,1)$ and $s_0 = 1/2$. Let
    58	  $k_f(s_0) = \int_0^1|s_0-t|^{-a}f(t)\ud t > 0$. The smooth test $\Psi(t,x) =
    59	  cf(t)z(x)/k_f(s_0)$ has mean $cU_z$ at $s_0$.
    60	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate} gives boundedness of this
    61	  potential, the displayed real Rayleigh formula, and a positive rate for every
    62	  $c > 0$. Comparing identical unit tests makes $\lambda_z(c)^2$ Lipschitz with
    63	  constant $\|U_z\|_\infty$. On a positive compact interval its rate has a
    64	  positive floor by monotonicity, giving the square-root Lipschitz bound.
    65	
    66	  Use the nonincreasing smooth cutoff $\chi$ constructed in the proof of
    67	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-remove-mask}. For integers $n \ge 4$, set on
    68	  $(0,1)$
    69	  \[
    70	    f_n(t)=f_a(t)\chi(1/(nt))\chi(1/(n(1-t))),\qquad
    71	    k_n(s)=\int_0^1|s-t|^{-a}f_n(t)\ud t.
    72	  \]
    73	  Extend $f_n$ by zero. It is smooth compact, vanishes near both endpoints, is
    74	  nonzero, and increases to $f_a$. Thus, $\Psi_n = f_n\otimes z$ is a positive
    75	  smooth control. Monotone convergence
    76	  and~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-potential} give $k_n(s)\uparrow1$ for every
    77	  $s \in [0,1]$. Since the kernel is at least one on the unit square off its
    78	  null diagonal, $0 < c_0: = \int_0^1f_4 \le k_n(s) \le 1$. The mean is
    79	  $k_n(s)U_z$; hence its rate is $\lambda_z(k_n(s))$, converging to
    80	  $\lambda_z(1)$ and bounded by that finite number. Dominated convergence gives
    81	  $I_{\Psi_n} \to \lambda_z(1)$.
    82	
    83	  The Gaussian cost is exactly the nonnegative Tonelli pairing
    84	  \[
    85	    v_{\Psi_n}=B_\Gamma(z,z)\int_0^1f_n(s)k_n(s)\ud s.
    86	  \]
    87	  Its time integrand increases to $f_a$, so the cost tends to
    88	  $M_aB_\Gamma(z,z)$. The spatial factor is finite and positive: its smooth
    89	  compact autocorrelation is positive near zero, and homogeneity scales any
    90	  origin-centered ball of positive $\Gamma$ mass to every other positive radius.
    91	  Such a ball exists by exhaustion. Take the limit of the individual
    92	  inequalities $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}} \ge I_{\Psi_n}-v_{\Psi_n}/2$. The variational
    93	  expression differences need not increase. No control depends on original large
    94	  time and no rough stochastic evolution has been used. This proves
    95	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls}.
    96	\end{proof}
    97	
    98	The next estimate also allows zero covariance and does not use the finiteness
    99	of $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$.
   100	
   166	\begin{proposition}[The finite smooth spatial ratio]
   167	  \label{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}
   168	  For real unit $g \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$ put $R(g) =
   169	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)/b(g)^{\alpha/2}$. Its supremum $R_0$ over these profiles is
   170	  a positive finite real number, and
   171	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-smooth-score}
   172	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge

  3653	    \left\|\prod_{j=1}^n\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)\right\|_2
  3654	    \le\prod_{j=1}^n\|\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)\|_{2n}
  3655	    \le\sqrt{(2n-1)!!}\,V^{n/2}.

  3658	  fixed finite $L^p$. Hence, the product is strongly measurable in $L^2$ on the
  3659	  stated pieces. The finite kernel mass and the displayed bound prove Bochner
  3660	  integrability and~\eqref{E:terminal-term-majorant}.

  3663	  measures. For the $m+n$ Gaussian variables at their labelled vertices,
  3664	  differentiate
  3665	  \[
  3666	    \E\exp\left(\sum_i t_i\mathcal{W}(\tau_i,\eta_i)\right)
  3667	    =\exp\left(\frac12\sum_{i,j}t_i t_j
  3668	    \mathcal{K}(\tau_i,\eta_i;\tau_j,\eta_j)\right)
  3669	  \]

  3671	  result is the sum over unordered pair partitions, with one covariance product
  3672	  per pairing. Orientations and orderings of the $k$ pairs cancel the
  3673	  exponential's $2^k k!$ denominator. Integration
  3674	  gives~\eqref{E:terminal-wick-formula} with precisely the domains and
  3675	  coefficients in~\eqref{E:terminal-pairing-integral}.

  3677	  Symmetrizing a chain measure does not change its stochastic integral: the
  3678	  product of its $n$ scalar field values is invariant under relabeling. Thus,

  3681	  in~\eqref{E:terminal-wick-formula}, or $m!n!$ in a two-chain product. This
  3682	  identifies the ordinary ordered regularized integrals and their symmetrized
  3683	  convention in~\eqref{E:expansion}.

  3686	  measures have the same masses and converge weakly to $G$. Off the finitely
  3687	  many time cut points, all finite Gaussian moments are bounded continuous
  3688	  functions of the spatial variables. Dominated convergence for their finite
  3689	  Wick sums proves the same limit for the mixed second moments with two Green

  3694	  product nonnegative. Comparing them proves the stated finite-moment
  3695	  monotonicity, including self-pairs and unequal chains. Finally, the ratio of

  3701	\subsection{Removing the regularization}
  3702	
  3703	\begin{lemma}[Uniform series tails from scaled moments]\label{L:uniform-series-tail}
  3704	  Fix $(T,x)$. For each positive regularization pair $(\epsilon,\delta)$, let
  3705	  $Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}$ be the terms of Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick} for a
  3706	  field with nonnegative covariance. Write $u^{\epsilon,\delta}(r) =
  3707	  \sum_{n\ge0}r^nY_n^{\epsilon,\delta}$. Suppose that, for some $r > 1$ and
  3708	  finite $B_r$,
  3709	  \[
  3710	    \sup_{\epsilon,\delta>0}
  3711	    \E|u^{\epsilon,\delta}(r)|^2\le B_r,
  3712	    \qquad
  3713	    Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\longrightarrow X_n
  3714	    \text{ in }L^2\text{ for each fixed }n.
  3715	  \]
  3716	  Then $u = \sum_{n\ge0}X_n$ converges absolutely in $L^2$,
  3717	  $u^{\epsilon,\delta}(1) \to u$ in $L^2$, and
  3718	  \begin{equation}\label{E:uniform-series-tail}
  3719	    \|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\|_2,\ \|X_n\|_2
  3720	    \le B_r^{1/2}r^{-n},\qquad
  3721	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\right\|_2,
  3722	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}X_n\right\|_2
  3723	    \le\frac{B_r^{1/2}r^{-(N+1)}}{1-r^{-1}}.
  3724	  \end{equation}
  3725	  If also $\E|u^{\epsilon,\delta}(1)|^2 \le B_1$ uniformly, then $\E|u|^2 \le
  3726	  B_1$.
  3727	\end{lemma}
  3728	
  3729	\begin{proof}
  3730	  Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick} gives absolute $L^2$ convergence of every
  3731	  regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. Its scaled second moment
  3732	  therefore contains the nonnegative term $r^{2n}\E|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}|^2$,
  3733	  so $r^{2n}\E|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}|^2 \le B_r$. Taking the fixed-order $L^2$
  3734	  limit proves the same bound for $X_n$. The geometric series and the triangle
  3735	  inequality give all estimates in~\eqref{E:uniform-series-tail}, including
  3736	  absolute convergence.
  3737	
  3738	  For each $N$, write both full series as their first $N+1$ terms and their
  3739	  tails. Their distance is at most
  3740	  \[
  3741	    \frac{2B_r^{1/2}r^{-(N+1)}}{1-r^{-1}}
  3742	    +\left\|\sum_{n=0}^N(Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}-X_n)\right\|_2.
  3743	  \]
  3744	  First let $\epsilon,\delta\downarrow0$ at fixed $N$, and then let $N \to
  3745	  \infty$. This proves convergence of the full regularized solution; it was not
  3746	  assumed. Continuity of the $L^2$ norm passes the bound $B_1$ to $u$. This
  3747	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:uniform-series-tail}.
  3748	\end{proof}
  4691	We now retain Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} with $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha
  4692	\le 1$. The covariance is nonnegative and nonnegative definite as in
  4693	Section~\ref{S:model}; when it is a distribution, both these properties and its
  4694	homogeneity are understood distributionally. Let $\mu$ be its positive Radon
  4695	spectral measure in the convention $\gamma(x) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot
  4696	x}\mu(\ud\xi)$, and put $V = \mu(\{\xi:|\xi|\le1\})$. No isotropy or spectral
  4697	density is assumed. Write $G_h$ for the positive wave-kernel measure of mass
  4698	$h$, and $G_{h,\eta} = p_\eta*G_h$ for $\eta > 0$; set $G_{h,0} = G_h$. The
  4699	measure notation includes the sphere kernel in dimension three. The mixed-moment
  4700	definition of $A_k(t)$ is now applied to the present $d$-dimensional solution.
  4701	
  4702	\begin{lemma}[Low-$\alpha$ convolution bound]\label{L:low-alpha-convolution}
  4703	  Under the preceding assumptions with $0 < \alpha < 1$, for every $R,h > 0$,
  4704	  \begin{equation}\label{E:low-alpha-radial}
  4705	    \mu(\{\xi:|\xi|\le R\})=VR^\alpha,\qquad
  4706	    \int_{\R^d}\min\{h,|\xi|^{-1}\}\mu(\ud\xi)
  4707	    =\frac{V}{1-\alpha}h^{1-\alpha}.
  4708	  \end{equation}
  4709	  For $\epsilon > 0$ and $\eta \ge 0$,
  4710	  \begin{equation}\label{E:low-alpha-convolution}
  4711	    0\le\int_{\R^d}G_{h,\eta}(\ud y)\gamma_\epsilon(y+z)
  4712	    \le\frac{V}{1-\alpha}h^{1-\alpha},
  4713	    \qquad z\in\R^d.
  4714	  \end{equation}
  4715	  The estimate is uniform in both smoothing parameters and in $z$.
  4716	\end{lemma}
  4717	
  4718	\begin{proof}
  4719	  The spectral measure of $\gamma(c\,\cdot)$ is the pushforward of $\mu$ under
  4720	  $\xi\mapsto c\xi$. Homogeneity and uniqueness of the Fourier transform on
  4721	  tempered distributions therefore give $\mu(A/c) = c^{-\alpha}\mu(A)$ for every
  4722	  Borel set $A$. Equivalently, $\mu(cA) = c^\alpha\mu(A)$. This proves the
  4723	  ball-mass formula. Since $\mu$ is Radon, $V < \infty$, and continuity from
  4724	  above gives $\mu(\{0\}) = \lim_{R\downarrow0}VR^\alpha = 0$. By the layer-cake
  4725	  identity and Tonelli's theorem,
  4726	  \[
  4727	    \int_{\R^d}\min\{h,|\xi|^{-1}\}\mu(\ud\xi)
  4728	    =\int_0^h\mu(\{\xi:|\xi|\le u^{-1}\})\ud u
  4729	    =V\int_0^h u^{-\alpha}\ud u.
  4730	  \]
  4731	  The endpoint of each indicator has no effect on its $u$ integral. Since
  4732	  $\alpha < 1$, the last expression is the finite quantity
  4733	  in~\eqref{E:low-alpha-radial}. This computation uses ball masses, not a radial
  4734	  density for $\mu$.
  4735	
  4736	  Gaussian weighting gives a finite measure, by the polynomial ball growth of
  4737	  $\mu$. Thus, Fourier Fubini is justified for $\gamma_\epsilon$ and the finite
  4738	  measure $G_{h,\eta}$. From the source's wave-kernel
  4739	  formulas~\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{(2.3)--(2.5), p.~7},
  4740	  \[
  4741	    \widehat{G}_h(\xi)=\frac{\sin(h|\xi|)}{|\xi|},\qquad
  4742	    G_h(\R^d)=h,
  4743	  \]
  4744	  with value $h$ in the Fourier formula at zero. The Fourier multipliers of
  4745	  $p_\epsilon$ and $p_\eta$ have absolute value at most one, with the latter
  4746	  multiplier equal to one when $\eta = 0$. Consequently,
  4747	  \[
  4748	    \left|\int G_{h,\eta}(\ud y)\gamma_\epsilon(y+z)\right|
  4749	    \le\int_{\R^d}\frac{|\sin(h|\xi|)|}{|\xi|}\mu(\ud\xi)
  4750	    \le\int_{\R^d}\min\{h,|\xi|^{-1}\}\mu(\ud\xi).
  4751	  \]
  4752	  Nonnegativity of $\gamma$ as a distribution implies $\gamma_\epsilon \ge 0$,
  4753	  since Gaussian translates are nonnegative test functions; $G_{h,\eta}$ is also
  4754	  nonnegative. This proves the lower bound in~\eqref{E:low-alpha-convolution}.
  4755	  Combining the preceding displays proves its upper bound. No positivity of the
  4756	  oscillatory Fourier integrand is asserted. This proves
  4757	  Lemma~\ref{L:low-alpha-convolution}.

2046	A time-block argument would have to carry both position and velocity. We
  2047	establish a uniform estimate for the first variance coefficient with arbitrary
  2048	deterministic initial phase. The covariance may be any member of the original
  2049	three-dimensional class; no endpoint representation is assumed. The estimate
  2050	below is not an all-order propagator bound.
  2051	
  2052	
  2053	
  2054	Let $0 < \alpha < 2$, and let $\Gamma$ be a nonnegative, even, positive-definite
  2055	tempered Radon covariance on $\R^3$, satisfying $\Gamma(rA) =
  2056	r^{3-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$. Its spectral convention is $\Gamma = \int e^{i\xi\cdot
  2057	x}\mu(\ud\xi)$. Put
  2058	\begin{equation}\label{E:phase-constants}
  2059	  \begin{split}
  2060	    V&=\mu(B_1),\qquad M=\Gamma(B_1),\qquad
  2061	    R_\alpha=\frac{\alpha\pi V}{2\sin(\pi\alpha/2)},\\
  2062	    c_\Gamma&=\frac{(3-\alpha)M}{4\pi},\qquad
  2063	    b_\alpha=2^\alpha+\frac{3^{2-\alpha}}{2-\alpha},\qquad
  2064	    D_\Gamma=c_\Gamma b_\alpha.
  2065	  \end{split}
  2066	\end{equation}
  2067	Here $B_1$ is the open unit ball in the relevant variable. The physical mass $M$
  2068	and the spectral mass $V$ are not identified. Let $p_\epsilon$ be the Brownian
  2069	Gaussian density with covariance $\epsilon I$, and set $\Gamma_\epsilon =
  2070	p_{2\epsilon}*\Gamma$.
  2071	
  2072	\begin{lemma}[Two static contraction bounds]\label{L:phase-contractions}
  2073	  For $\lambda > 0$, $q \in \R^3$, $a > 0$, and $\epsilon > 0$,
  2074	  \begin{align}
  2075	    \int_{\R^3}\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{\lambda^2+|q+\xi|^2}
  2076	    &\le R_\alpha\lambda^{\alpha-2},
  2077	    \label{E:phase-resolvent}\\
  2078	    \left|T_\epsilon(a,q)\right|
  2079	    &\le D_\Gamma a^{1-\alpha},
  2080	    \label{E:phase-trace}\\
  2081	    T_\epsilon(a,q)
  2082	    &:=\int_{\R^3}e^{iq\cdot x}\Gamma_\epsilon(x)G_a(\ud x)
  2083	    =\int_{\R^3}\widehat{G}_a(q+\xi)e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2}
  2084	    \mu(\ud\xi).\nonumber
  2085	  \end{align}
  2086	\end{lemma}
  2087	
  2088	\begin{proof}
  2089	  Homogeneity and Fourier uniqueness give $\mu(B_r) = Vr^\alpha$. In particular,
  2090	  there is no origin atom. For $s > 0$, Schwartz Fourier pairing yields
  2091	  \[
  2092	    \int e^{-s|q+\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
  2093	    =\int p_{2s}(x)e^{iq\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x)
  2094	    \le\int p_{2s}(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
  2095	    =\int e^{-s|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi).
  2096	  \]
  2097	  The integrals are finite. Evenness makes the middle integral real, and
  2098	  nonnegativity of $\Gamma$ gives the inequality. Multiply by $e^{-\lambda^2s}$
  2099	  and integrate in $s$. Nonnegative Tonelli on the spectral side gives the
  2100	  resolvent comparison. At $q = 0$ its value is
  2101	  \[
  2102	    \alpha V\int_0^\infty\frac{r^{\alpha-1}}{\lambda^2+r^2}\ud r
  2103	    =R_\alpha\lambda^{\alpha-2}.
  2104	  \]
  2105	  This proves~\eqref{E:phase-resolvent}.
  2106	
  2107	  Since $\mu$ is tempered, its Gaussian weighting is finite. Fourier Fubini
  2108	  therefore gives the identity for $T_\epsilon$. The measure
  2109	  $\Gamma_\epsilon(x)G_a(\ud x)$ is finite and nonnegative, whence
  2110	  $|T_\epsilon(a,q)| \le T_\epsilon(a,0)$. The radial distribution function of
  2111	  $\Gamma$ is $\Gamma(B_r) = Mr^{3-\alpha}$. Thus, for every nonnegative radial
  2112	  Schwartz function $F$,
  2113	  \[
  2114	    \int F(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
  2115	    =(3-\alpha)M\int_0^\infty F(r)r^{2-\alpha}\ud r
  2116	    =c_\Gamma\int_{\R^3}F(x)|x|^{-\alpha}\ud x.
  2117	  \]
  2118	  Apply this to $F = G_a*p_{2\epsilon}$, which is radial and Schwartz.
  2119	  Nonnegative Fubini gives
  2120	  \[
  2121	    T_\epsilon(a,0)
  2122	    =c_\Gamma[p_{2\epsilon}*(G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})](0)
  2123	    \le c_\Gamma\sup_z(G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})(z).
  2124	  \]
  2125	  Write $r = |z|$. The spherical wave measure has mass $a$, and direct
  2126	  integration over its normal coordinate gives, for $r > 0$,
  2127	  \[
  2128	    (G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})(z)
  2129	    =\frac{(a+r)^{2-\alpha}-|a-r|^{2-\alpha}}
  2130	    {2r(2-\alpha)}.
  2131	  \]
  2132	  For $r < a/2$, distances from $z$ to the sphere are at least $a/2$, giving the
  2133	  bound $2^\alpha a^{1-\alpha}$. For $r > 2a$, they are at least $a$, giving
  2134	  $a^{1-\alpha}$. On $a/2 \le r \le 2a$, the displayed formula is at most
  2135	  $3^{2-\alpha}a^{1-\alpha}/(2-\alpha)$. These bounds also cover the endpoints
  2136	  by continuity and give~\eqref{E:phase-trace}. This proves
  2137	  Lemma~\ref{L:phase-contractions}.
  2138	\end{proof}
  2577	\begin{proposition}[All regularized static phase orders]
  2578	  \label{P:static-phase-all-orders}
  2579	  Retain the full covariance class of Section~\ref{S:static-phase}. For real
  2580	  Schwartz $f,g$, let $Z_n^\epsilon(h)$ be the $n$th regularized static Duhamel
  2581	  phase, with the recursion \eqref{E:phase-duhamel} for every $n \ge 0$. This is
  2582	  an ordinary Gaussian polynomial of degree at most $n$, including
  2583	  self-contractions; it is not a pure Wick chaos. There is an explicit finite
  2584	  constant
  2585	  \[
  2586	    A_\alpha=\frac{400\sqrt2\,e^2}{\delta_{\alpha/2}}
  2587	  \]
  2588	  such that, for $n \ge 1$, uniformly in $\epsilon > 0$,
  2589	  \begin{equation}\label{E:all-static-phase-orders}
  2590	    \|Z_n^\epsilon(h)\|_{L^2(\Omega;X_{1/h})}
  2591	    \le
  2592	    \frac{(A_\alpha\sqrt{R_\alpha})^n
  2593	    h^{(4-\alpha)n/2}}{(n!)^{(3-\alpha)/2}}
  2594	    \|(f,g)\|_{1/h}.
  2595	  \end{equation}

  2597	  $\sum_{n\ge0}\sigma^nZ_n^\epsilon(h)$ converges in $L^2$ phase. Its squared
  2598	  norm is at most
  2599	  \begin{equation}\label{E:all-static-phase-sum}
  2600	    (\sqrt e+2)^2
  2601	    \exp\left\{6A_\alpha^{2/(3-\alpha)}
  2602	    (|\sigma|^2R_\alpha)^{1/(3-\alpha)}
  2603	    h^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}\right\}\|(f,g)\|_{1/h}^2.
  2604	  \end{equation}
  2605	\end{proposition}

  2618	  formula for their operator-valued series bounds the $n$th coefficient by

  2620	    100e^{2\lambda h}
  2621	    \left(\frac{d_N}
  2622	    {\delta_{\alpha/2}\lambda^{2-\alpha/2}}\right)^n
  2623	    \|S_b(f,g)\|_\lambda .
  2624	  \]
  2625	  The coefficient is exactly the $n$th Duhamel phase from the vacuum. Apply
  2626	  Lemma~\ref{L:finite-word-cutoff} with one color, $N = n$, the spatial phase
  2627	  Hilbert space as $\mathscr{X}$, and its free wave operators as the $F_l$. It
  2628	  identifies each cutoff Duhamel word exactly with its uncompressed word,
  2629	  including self-contractions. Dominated time integration preserves this
  2630	  identity.
  2631	
  2632	  Choose $\lambda = n/h$. For any phase $z$, $\|z\|_{1/h} \le n\|z\|_{n/h}$ and
  2633	  $\|(f,g)\|_{n/h} \le \|(f,g)\|_{1/h}$. Also $d_n \le
  2634	  2\sqrt{2n}\sqrt{R_\alpha}$. The preceding bound is therefore at most
  2635	  \[
  2636	    100n\left(\frac{2\sqrt2 e^2}{\delta_{\alpha/2}}\right)^n
  2637	    R_\alpha^{n/2}h^{(4-\alpha)n/2}
  2638	    n^{-(3-\alpha)n/2}\|(f,g)\|_{1/h}.
  2639	  \]
  2640	  Since $100n \le 200^n$ and $n! \le n^n$, this gives
  2641	  \eqref{E:all-static-phase-orders} at the cutoffs.
  2642	
  2643	  We justify removal of those cutoffs at fixed $\epsilon$ and $n$. On Gaussian
  2644	  degrees at most $N$, the unweighted field multiplication has norm at most
  2645	  $2\sqrt{N+1}\sqrt{v_\epsilon}$, uniformly in $m$, by the same
  2646	  creation/annihilation argument applied pointwise in $x$. It follows that the
  2647	  noise phase insertion $(u,v)\mapsto(0,W_\epsilon u)$, between the required
  2648	  finite degree levels, is bounded on $X_\lambda$ by this constant divided by
  2649	  $\lambda$. Free phase evolution is bounded by $e^{\lambda h/2}$. For finite
  2650	  $m$, $S_b \to I$ strongly and commutes with the free propagator. Each fixed

  2654	  Next let $m \to \infty$ on the full Gaussian space. The truncated field
  2655	  multiplications converge strongly between finite degree levels. To see this,
  2656	  first take a vector depending on finitely many Gaussian coordinates. The
  2657	  annihilation tail is then zero, while the creation tail is bounded by a
  2658	  constant times

  2660	    \left(\int\sum_{i>m}e_i(x)^2\|F(x)\|^2\ud x\right)^{1/2},
  2661	  \]

  2681	  \eqref{E:all-static-phase-sum}. This proves
  2682	  Proposition~\ref{P:static-phase-all-orders}.
  2683	\end{proof}

"""Index-by-label category check (R5 replaced by the per-declaration rules R6-R12) (scratch tool, not part of the repo).
Usage: index_category_check.py WT [--verbose]
Rules:
 R1 the first parenthesized qualifier of every Index first cell starts with
    one of: "whole result", "narrower result", "foundation", "proof steps".
 R2 "whole result" needs the label's coverage row to be conclusion full, or
    (no coverage row and every module of the row is a whole-result section).
 R3 "narrower result" needs the label's coverage row not full (or no row), and
    some module of the row in a narrower-result section, unless the cell says
    "override".
 R4 a cell all of whose modules are foundation/proof-step sections may not say
    "whole result" or "narrower result" unless it says "override".
 R5 "nothing supplied" may not cover a theorem whose Lean binders take a named
    analytic input; "inputs supplied" may not cover a theorem whose binders take
    none, unless the cell names the declaration as input-free ("input-free").
"""
import re,sys,yaml,glob,os,collections
wt=sys.argv[1]; verbose='--verbose' in sys.argv
CATS=('whole result','narrower result','foundation','proof steps')
INPUTS=['GreenMass','GreenFourier','FockColumn','WaveFourierThree','ArchimedesLaw','H1TestDense','InventoryProduct',
 'SquarePairingBounds','SpaceTimeCS','RayleighFloor','OccupationCeilingK0','SquareBound','StaticControls','S1Bdd',
 'TerminalWickInput','RawBlockOriginalLower','TypeContinuityInputs','LeftYoungSumsConverge','FreeWaveData']
NAMED_BINDERS=['hmem','hnorm','hmod','hsm','hlink','hmeas','hcircle','hentire','hband','hgauss','hsplits','hfixed','hRB',
 'hborn','hmean','hY0','hY','hodd','hcoef','henergy','hZ0','hZ','hcol','hQ','hJ','hCPC','hCPF','hCPH','hJL2','hnormSG','hdense']
EXTRA={'ClockCopyHomog':'A','MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted':'A','TimeSchur':'A','DampedNorms':'C','SpectralHomog':'C',
 'TimeFractional':'C','WaveKernel':'C','GaussianIBP':'C','GaussianTest':'C','WeakSobolev':'C'}
led=open(wt+'/docs/statement-ledger.md').read().split('\n')
sec={}
for l in led:
    m=re.match(r'## (\w+) \((.*)\)$',l)
    if m:
        t=m.group(2)
        sec[m.group(1)]='A' if t.startswith('whole result') else 'B' if t.startswith('narrower') else 'C'
sec.update(EXTRA)
cov={}
for r in yaml.safe_load(open(wt+'/coverage.yaml'))['rows']:
    cov[r['paper']['label']]=r.get('conclusion') or ('full' if r['class']!='outside' else None)
claims={c['decl']:c for c in yaml.safe_load(open(wt+'/claims.yaml'))['claims']}
src={}
def sig(full):
    c=claims.get(full)
    if not c: return None,None
    f=wt+'/'+c['file']
    if f not in src: src[f]=open(f).read()
    short=full.split('.')[-1]
    m=re.search(r'^(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)?(?:private\s+|protected\s+|noncomputable\s+)*(theorem|lemma|def|abbrev|structure|instance)\s+(?:[\w.]*\.)?'+re.escape(short)+r'\b(.*?)(?=:=|\bwhere\b|^\s*$)',src[f],re.M|re.S)
    if not m: return c['kind'],''

def binders_inputs(s):
    hits=set()

        if re.search(r'\(\s*[\w\']+(?:\s+[\w\']+)*\s*:\s*(?:[\w.]*\.)?'+n+r'\b',s): hits.add(n)
    for b in NAMED_BINDERS:

    return hits

probs=[]; n=0
for k in range(i0,i1):
    l=led[k]
    if not l.startswith('| ') or l.startswith('| Paper label') or l.startswith('|---'): continue
    parts=re.split(r'(?<!\\)\|',l.strip()[1:-1]); c0=parts[0].strip(); c1=parts[1].strip()
    n+=1
    if c1.startswith('all declarations of'):
        if not re.match(r'no direct label \((foundation|proof steps)',c0): probs.append((k+1,'R1 aggregate row without category',c0[:90]))
        continue
    lm=re.match(r'(`[^`]+`|no direct label)\s*(.*)$',c0)
    lab=lm.group(1).strip('`'); rest=lm.group(2)
    q=re.match(r'\(([^()]*(?:\([^()]*\)[^()]*)*)',rest)
    qual=q.group(1) if q else ''
    cat=next((c for c in CATS if qual.startswith(c)),None)
    line=k+1
    if not cat: probs.append((line,'R1 no category',c0[:90])); continue
    decls=re.findall(r'`([\w.\']+)`',c1)
    mods=set()
    fulls=[]
    for d in decls:
        mod=d.split('.')[0]
        full=('StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.' if 'StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.'+d in claims else 'StratonovichHAMAudit.')+d

import subprocess,json as _json,os as _os

_rows={r['line']:r for r in _T['rows']}
_by=collections.defaultdict(list)
for d in _T['decls']: _by[d['line']].append(d)

    if len(inps)>1: probs.append((line,'R7 row mixes input sets %s'%sorted(inps),cell[:80]))
    if 'definition' in kinds and cat in ('whole result','narrower result'): probs.append((line,'R8 definitions in a whole/narrower row',cell[:80]))
    if cat in ('whole result','narrower result') and any(d['statement'] for d in ds) and any(not d['statement'] for d in ds if d['kind']=='theorem'):

    for x in (sorted(inps)[0] if len(inps)==1 else ()):

        probs.append((line,'R12 inputs supplied but no declaration takes a named input',cell[:80]))
import collections as _c
for p in probs: print('%d: %s | %s'%p)
print('cells checked: %d; problems: %d'%(n,len(probs)))

   777	Write $G_\theta(s,y) = e^{-\theta s}G(s,y)$ and $\widehat{G}_s(\xi) =
   778	\sin(s|\xi|)/|\xi|$, with value $s$ at $\xi = 0$. We use the norms in the
   779	source's (3.3)--(3.5), with the full covariance, but give their bounds directly.
   780	Write $\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}$ for Euler's Gamma function in the following
   781	definitions, to distinguish it from the covariance measure:
   782	\begin{equation}\label{E:damped-norm-definitions}
   783	  \begin{split}
   784	    N_0(\theta)&=\int_0^\infty e^{-\theta s}G_s(\R^d)\ud s,\\
   785	    N_1(\theta)&=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   786	    \int_0^\infty\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda
   787	    \int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{(\theta+\lambda)^2+|\xi|^2},\\
   788	    N_2(\theta)^2&=\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty
   789	    e^{-\theta(s+t)}|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}
   790	    \int\widehat{G}_s(\xi)\overline{\widehat{G}_t(\xi)}
   791	    \mu(\ud\xi)\ud s\ud t.
   792	  \end{split}
   793	\end{equation}
   794	The second expression uses the elementary wave Laplace transform $\int_0^\infty
   795	e^{-as}\widehat{G}_s(\xi)\ud s = (a^2+|\xi|^2)^{-1}$. The last expression is the
   796	space-time covariance quadratic form; in physical variables it pairs
   797	$G_\theta(s,x)$ with $G_\theta(t,y)$. Thus, the second Green factor in the
   798	printed source (3.5) is read with the independent variable $y$; see
   799	Lemma~\ref{L:translated-covariance-CS} and
   800	Remark~\ref{R:source-case2-time-shift} for the independent justification and the
   801	exact source qualification.
   802	
   803	\begin{lemma}[Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails]
   804	  \label{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}
   805	  Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, the integrals
   806	  in~\eqref{E:damped-norm-definitions} are finite for every $\theta > 0$, with
   807	  $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$, and
   808	  \[
   809	    N_0(\theta)=\theta^{-2},\qquad
   810	    N_1(\theta)=\theta^{\alpha+\alpha_0-2}N_1(1),\qquad
   811	    N_2(\theta)^2=\theta^{-\beta}N_2(1)^2,
   812	    \quad\beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0.
   813	  \]
   814	  Let
   815	  \[
   816	    K_M(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   817	    \int_M^\infty e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
   818	  \]
   819	  Denote by $N_1^{(M)}(1)$ the first norm with $\lambda > M$, and by
   820	  $N_2^{(M)}(1)$ the second norm with $K_M(s-t)$ in place of
   821	  $|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}$. Then
   822	  \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-tail-norms}
   823	    N_1^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0,\qquad
   824	    N_2^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0\quad(M\to\infty).
   825	  \end{equation}
   826	  More precisely, let $m:\R^d\to[0,1]$ be measurable and let
   827	  $S\subset S'\subset(0,\infty)$ be measurable. Define $N_{1,m,S}(\theta)$
   828	  by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$ and restricting the $\lambda$ integral in
   829	  $N_1$ to $S$. Define $N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2$ by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$
   830	  and the temporal kernel in $N_2^2$ with
   831	  \[
   832	    K_S(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   833	    \int_S e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
   834	  \]
   835	  Then, for every $\theta>0$,
   836	  \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-multiplier-comparison}
   837	    \begin{split}
   838	      0\le N_{1,m,S}(\theta)&\le N_{1,1,S'}(\theta),\\
   839	      0\le N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2&\le N_{2,1,S'}(\theta)^2.
   840	    \end{split}
   841	  \end{equation}
   842	  These are comparisons of spectral expressions, including full and tail
   843	  domains. An arbitrary $m$ need not preserve Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}; the
   844	  scaling identities above are asserted for the original covariance only.
   845	  Spatial Gaussian smoothing and Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel
   846	  give multipliers in this class. The separate mass identity for $N_0$ is

  2289	  Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $A_0$ a bounded nonnegative selfadjoint
  2290	  operator, and $B$ a bounded selfadjoint operator. Write $A_\rho = \rho^2+A_0$.
  2291	  Suppose that, for $0 < a < 1$ and $d > 0$,
  2292	  \begin{equation}\label{E:abstract-sandwich}
  2293	    \|A_\rho^{-1/2}BA_\rho^{-1/2}\|\le d\rho^{a-2},
  2294	    \qquad \rho>0.
  2295	  \end{equation}
  2296	  Put
  2297	  \[
  2298	    I_a=\int_0^\infty s^{-1/2}(1+s)^{(a-3)/2}\ud s,\qquad
  2299	    \delta_a=\min\{1/4,\pi/(8I_a)\}.
  2300	  \]
  2301	  For $\lambda > 0$ and $|z| \le \delta_a\lambda^{2-a}/d$, let $L = A_0-zB$. The
  2302	  phase propagator of $u''+Lu = 0$ satisfies
  2303	  \begin{equation}\label{E:complex-phase-bound}
  2304	    \|\mathcal{M}_z(h)\|_{X_\lambda\to X_\lambda}
  2305	    \le100e^{2\lambda h},\qquad
  2306	    \|(f,g)\|_{X_\lambda}^2
  2307	    =\|f\|^2+\|A_\lambda^{-1/2}g\|^2,\quad h\ge0.
  2308	  \end{equation}

  2473	  Retain the covariance and $R_\alpha$ of Section~\ref{S:static-phase}. Fix

  2475	  Gaussian coordinates as $W_\epsilon(x) = \sum_{i\ge1}g_i e_i(x)$ in
  2476	  $L^2(\Omega)$. Let $P_N$ be projection onto Gaussian Hermite degrees at most
  2477	  $N$, and $S_b$ spatial Fourier projection onto $|\eta| \le b$. For finite $m$,
  2478	  on their joint range set
  2479	  \[
  2480	    B_{N,m,b}=P_NS_b\Big(\sum_{i=1}^m g_i M_{e_i}\Big)S_bP_N,\qquad

  2483	  These are bounded selfadjoint operators and, uniformly in $\epsilon,m,b$,
